tasks.title: Replace the battery of a TV remote
tasks.description: With a dexterous hand (Sharpa Wave by default, or Wuji Hand 2.2) slide open a remote's battery door, move the old gray AA cell from its slot into a receiving tray, seat a new green AA cell with correct polarity and slide the door shut; drops, knock-offs and a displaced remote fail the episode at once.
tasks.mechanism: passive sliding battery door with friction detent, free AA cells, free remote and tray
tasks.instruction: Replace the battery of a TV remote that lies on the table. The remote's sliding battery door is closed over a one-cell compartment holding an old gray AA cell; a new green AA cell lies on the table and an empty receiving tray stands beside the remote. In this order: (1) slide the door open until it is at least 0.060 m open (full travel 0.085 m); (2) move the gray cell out of the compartment into the tray, where it must rest on the tray floor: its centre inside the tray's inner box (|x| <= 0.037 m, |y| <= 0.032 m in the tray frame) and at most 0.014 m above the tray origin (the floor top is 0.003 m above the origin; a resting cell's centre is about 0.010 m above it), touching the tray floor, with no hand contact; (3) seat the green cell in the compartment slot with correct polarity: its centre within 5 mm (along the slot), 3 mm (across) and 2 mm (height) of the slot centre, lying on both cradle ribs, and its + end toward the gold contact (cell axis within 10 degrees of the remote's long axis, + end at the gold contact); (4) slide the door shut (at most 0.004 m open). Then release everything: with no hand contact on the remote, door, tray or either cell, the gray cell still in the tray, the green cell still seated, the door still shut and every task object at rest (linear speed of its body origin <= 0.02 m/s, angular speed <= 0.5 rad/s; for the cells and the tray the origin is the centre of mass), the condition must hold for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; each stage counts only after the previous ones, and partial completion never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 2 ms physics substep, when any cell, the door, the remote or the tray falls below the table top (z < 0.30 m) or leaves the workspace box x in [-0.37, 0.47] m, y in [-0.34, 0.34] m, z in [0.30, 0.80] m, when any of them touches the floor, when the remote slides more than 0.03 m or tilts more than 15 degrees, when the tray slides more than 0.03 m or tilts more than 15 degrees, when the gray cell touches the table top, when the green cell touches the table top again after it has been lifted (lifted: at a control it is clear of the table and its centre is more than 0.01 m above its start height), when a cell without hand contact moves down faster than 0.886 m/s (the speed of a free drop from 0.04 m), or a cell touching nothing at all (no hand, no surface) moves down faster than 0.5 m/s (there is no grace period; a later catch does not undo it), or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets are allowed; no object teleports, grasp welds, scripted object motion or direct object forces. The episode allows at most 6000 controls at 50 Hz; reaching that limit without success is a failure.
tasks.modeling: Free rigid remote (0.35 kg incl. ballast, rubber feet; the approved shell widened 1.25 times across for fingertip clearance), passive sliding battery door (slide joint, 0.085 m travel, end stops, 0.25 N friction hold, raised thumb ridge; the source's latch tab and compressible negative spring are not modelled), one-cell compartment with two cradle ribs between fixed end terminals (3 mm play), free rigid AA cells (23 g cylinders), free receiving tray. No electrical simulation.
